questions.questionText: All other things being equal, which one of the following is most likely to reduce the deficit on the UK’s balance of payments on current account?
options: A recovery in the world economy
A rise in the value of the pound
An increase in the price level in the UK
Rising real income levels for UK households

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a supply-side policy that is most likely to lead to an improvement in the balance of trade in goods and services on the current account of the UK’s balance of payments?
options: A significant and sustained reduction in Bank Rate by the Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of England
Deregulation that makes it easier for UK transnational corporations to invest abroad
Increasing the supply of pounds on the foreign exchange market to reduce the exchange rate and make exports cheaper
Tax breaks for manufacturing firms that invest in upgrading their machinery and other capital goods

questions.questionText: Explain factors that affect the UK’s balance of trade in motor vehicles.
All other things being equal, which one of the following is the most likely cause of a reduction in a country’s surplus on its balance of payments on current account?
options: A depreciation in the exchange rate
Contractionary fiscal policy
Falling labour productivity
Growth in export markets

questions.questionText: A government is concerned that aggregate demand is growing faster than the productive capacity of the economy. In addition, the deficit on its balance of payments on current account has worsened. Which one of the following policies is most likely to both reduce aggregate demand and help improve the balance of payments position?
options: A reduction in interest rates to cut mortgage repayments and lower the exchange rate
A reduction in taxes on company profits to encourage more innovation and investment
An increase in government borrowing to fund infrastructure spending and improve productivity
An increase in tax rates and a reduction in welfare payments to create a budget surplus

questions.questionText: Between October 2022 and July 2023, the value of the US Dollar (US$) in terms of the Swiss Franc (CHF) changed from US$ 1 = CHF 1 to US$ 1 = CHF 0.87. All other things being equal, this means that
options: the Swiss Franc and the US Dollar are no longer in equilibrium.
the Swiss Franc has become weaker against the US Dollar.
the volume of exports from Switzerland to the USA is likely to increase.
the volume of imports to Switzerland from the USA is likely to increase.

questions.questionText: Table 2 shows the UK's balance of trade in goods and services in successive quarters. What was the UK's median quarterly balance of trade over the period shown in Table 2?

A government introduces a number of supply-side policies that increase the size of the country's working population and labour productivity. All other things being equal, which one of the following statements identifies the most likely effects of the policies on the country's economy?
options: An increase in real national income and a reduction in the balance of payments deficit
An increase in short-run economic growth and inflation
An increase in the trend rate of economic growth and a growing balance of payments deficit
A reduction in unemployment and an increase in inflation

questions.questionText: Which one of the following helps to explain why, in a freely floating exchange rate system, market forces are likely to automatically reduce a deficit or surplus on a country's balance of trade?
options: A deficit will lead to excess demand for the country's currency and a depreciating exchange rate.
A deficit will lead to excess supply of the country's currency and an appreciating exchange rate.
A surplus will lead to excess demand for the country's currency and an appreciating exchange rate.
A surplus will lead to excess supply of the country's currency and a depreciating exchange rate.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is most likely to result in an increase in exports from the UK economy? An increase in
options: inflation in other countries.
productivity in other countries.
UK incomes.
UK interest rates.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following would be classified as a debit item in the secondary income section of the current account of the UK balance of payments?
options: Dividends paid to overseas owners of shares in UK companies
Emergency aid provided to another country following a natural disaster
Investment in building a factory abroad by a UK firm
Premiums paid by UK based organisations to foreign insurance companies

questions.questionText: Figure 8 shows the aggregate demand curve (AD) and the long-run aggregate supply curves (LRAS) for an economy. A redistribution of government spending from spending on welfare towards the funding of research and development shifts the long-run aggregate supply curve from LRAS1 to LRAS2. Which one of the following is the most likely effect of this policy?
options: A decrease in the number of people who are economically active
An improvement in the balance of payments on current account
An increase in the size of the government’s budget deficit
The creation of a positive output gap

questions.questionText: Explain how expenditure-switching policies can be used to reduce a deficit on a country’s balance of trade in goods and services.
Explain reasons for changes in the value of exports from the UK to the rest of the world.
An economy has a deficit on the current account of its balance of payments. Which one of the following sets of circumstances is most likely to cause the deficit to increase?
options: A depreciating exchange rate and lower unemployment
Better supply-side policies and lower interest rates
Expansionary fiscal policy and a stronger exchange rate
Increased labour productivity and lower interest rates

questions.questionText: Extract F (lines 7–8) states: ‘Economists said the data reinforced the view that the slump in South Korea’s trade-reliant economy would continue beyond this year’. Using the data in the extracts and your knowledge of economics, evaluate policies which could be used to boost South Korea’s exports and increase its trade surplus.
Which one of the following is an expenditure switching policy that would help to reduce a deficit on the balance of payments on current account? An increase in
options: government expenditure on public goods.
income tax to reduce consumer expenditure.
quotas on exports of demerit goods.
tariffs to raise the price of imports.

questions.questionText: Figure 8 shows two supply (S1 and S2) curves and the demand (D) curve for euros on the foreign exchange market and the price of euros in terms of pounds sterling. Which one of the following is the most likely explanation for the change in the exchange rate shown in Figure 8? An increase in eurozone
options: companies buying factories in the UK.
exports of manufactured goods to the UK.
interest rates relative to those in the UK.
productivity growth relative to that in the UK.

questions.questionText: The quantity of food imported by an economy increases by 12% in one year. The most likely cause is a fall in
options: domestic farm prices.
income tax.
the exchange rate.
welfare benefits.

questions.questionText: A government wishes to reduce the surplus on the current account of the balance of payments. Which one of the following sets of policies is likely to be the most successful?
Other things remaining the same, the current account deficit of an economy’s balance of payments is most likely to
options: become smaller as domestic inflation falls below foreign inflation rates.
deteriorate when there is an upturn in economic activity overseas.
improve when there is a rise in the exchange rate.
increase when there is an improvement in the economy’s international competitiveness.

questions.questionText: Table 1 shows the index of export prices, the current monetary value of a country’s exports and the calculated value, to the nearest £ billion, of the value of its exports at 2017 prices. Which one of the following is correct?
options: The value of the country’s exports in 2016 at 2017 prices, to the nearest £ billion, was £162 billion
The value of the country’s exports in 2016 at 2017 prices, to the nearest £ billion, was £198 billion
The value of the country’s exports in 2019 at 2017 prices, to the nearest £ billion, was £240 billion
The value of the country’s exports in 2019 at 2017 prices, to the nearest £ billion, was £250 billion

questions.questionText: If the current account of the balance of payments is in surplus, then
options: the exchange rate of the country’s currency must be appreciating.
the net value of trade in goods and services plus the net value of primary and secondary income must be positive.
the total of all money flows into the economy must be greater than the total of all money flows out.
the value of exports of goods and services must be greater than the value of imports of goods and services.

questions.questionText: The table below shows a selection of items from a country’s balance of payments on current account. If the country has a current account deficit of £84 billion, its balance of trade in services has a
options: deficit of £13 billion.
deficit of £40 billion.
surplus of £13 billion.
surplus of £40 billion.

questions.questionText: Assess the view that a depreciation of the pound against other currencies is likely to improve the UK’s macroeconomic performance.

An economy has a deficit on the current account of the balance of payments. Which one of the following sets of circumstances is most likely to lead to a reduction in the economy’s current account deficit?

The UK’s labour productivity increases by only 10% over a five year period. Over the same period its main trading partners increase their productivity by 25%. All other things being equal, the most likely consequence for the UK is
options: a decline in UK imports from its main trading partners.
a 15% deterioration in its balance of trade on the current account.
a loss of competitiveness against its main trading partners.
the imposition of a 15% tariff on imports to maintain international competitiveness.

questions.questionText: A country experiences a large net capital outflow. All other things being equal, the most likely consequence of this in the short run will be a decrease in
options: its exchange rate.
its net income from overseas investments.
its rate of interest.
the value of exports and imports.

questions.questionText: Extract B describes the trade figures as ‘disappointing’. Explain how the data in Extract A (Figure 2) show that the UK’s trade performance has been ‘disappointing’ given the fall in the value of the pound since November 2015.

Extract C (lines 8–9) states ‘Trade deficits and surpluses may be self-correcting in a floating exchange rate system.’ With the help of a diagram showing the supply of and demand for a currency, explain how a floating exchange rate may help to correct a trade surplus.

Extract B (lines 19–21) states ‘Although some argue that a current account deficit is not a problem, others point to the worryingly large and persistent nature of the deficit.’ Using the data in the extracts and your knowledge of economics, assess the impact of a persistent current account deficit on the macroeconomic performance of the UK economy.
A government reduces its budget deficit. Other things remaining the same, the most likely short-run impact of this policy is
options: a reduction in the current account deficit.
a reduction in unemployment.
an increase in the rate of economic growth.
an increase in the rate of inflation.

questions.questionText: A country has a deficit on the current account of its balance of payments. This means that
options: the country must have a deficit on the balance of trade in goods and services.
the net value of trade in goods and services plus the net value of primary and secondary income must be negative.
the value of all outflows from the country must be less than the value of all inflows.
the value of exports of goods must be less than the value of imports of goods.

questions.questionText: The table below shows selected components of the UK balance of payments on current account as a percentage of GDP between 2011 and 2014. It can be concluded from the data that between 2011 and 2014 the main reason for the rise in the current account deficit as a percentage of GDP was
options: GDP growing faster than the deficit on the current account.
the deficit on trade in goods increasing by more than the surplus on trade in services.
the deterioration in the primary income balance.
the growth in the deficit on the secondary income balance.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the measures that might be taken to reduce a deficit on the current account of the UK’s balance of payments.

An economy has a surplus on the current account of its balance of payments. Under which of the following circumstances is the economy most likely to experience a reduction in its current account surplus?
The current account of the balance of payments is in surplus. However, there are deficits on the balance of trade in goods and the balance of trade in services. It can be concluded that
options: the trade figures must be inaccurate.
the primary income (income flows) balance must be positive.
the combined primary and secondary income (income flows and transfers) balance must be positive.
the value of services exported must exceed the value of goods imported.
